candidate_relations.reason: Type I necrotizing fasciitis is a microbiologic subtype not established because cultures are not reported; missing tests are unknown, not Type I.
Fasciitis is the parent process but omits the required necrotizing soft-tissue infection.
Fournier gangrene is the accepted name for necrotizing fasciitis of the labia/perineum with subcutaneous gas extending to the groin and abdominal wall.
Bartholin abscess is a related vulvar infection but an incompatible non-necrotizing localized abscess versus gas-forming necrotizing fasciitis.
Necrotizing fasciitis matches the reference and the clinical decision for immediate exploration given subcutaneous gas and sepsis concern.
